title: Atomic Theory and Electron Configuration
seo_title: Chemistry 11: Atomic Theory and Electron Configuration Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Atoms and molecules are building blocks of matter: the development of atomic theory, the quantum mechanical model, electron configurations, isotopes and average atomic mass, and periodic trends. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Chemistry 11)
meta_desc: Free Chemistry 11 worksheets (BC Curriculum): atomic theory and electron configuration. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Electrons fill orbitals from lowest energy up.
body_html:
How to think about it

Atomic models changed with evidence: Dalton's solid spheres, Thomson's electrons, Rutherford's nucleus, Bohr's energy levels and the quantum mechanical model with orbitals (s, p, d, f). Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons; average atomic mass is weighted by abundance.

Electron configuration lists the orbitals in order of energy: O is 1s² 2s² 2p⁴. Valence electrons explain periodic trends: atomic radius decreases across a period and increases down a group; ionization energy and electronegativity do the opposite.

Example

Write the electron configuration of Na (11 electrons).

2 + 2 + 6 + 1

Answer: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s¹

Example

Which is larger: an Mg atom or a Cl atom?

Same period; radius decreases to the right.

Answer: Mg

Common mistakes

  • Filling 3d before 4s.
  • Thinking isotopes have different numbers of protons.
  • Thinking radius increases across a period.

faq.a: The nuclear charge increases while the shielding stays about the same, so electrons are held more tightly.
